4.text: they begin butchering and skinning them, leaving the heads with the skins

15.text: Next comes the painting with blood. First the people are painted, then

16.text: the sledges standing in line. Each family has its own hereditary style of

17.text: painting them. Among those that I saw, one had a line on the front part

18.text: of the runners, and a dot on each of the rear stanchions; another had a

19.text: straight line on the middle stanchion of the right side, a cross-line on both

20.text: front stanchions, and a dot on each of the runner-heads.

21.text: After the painting is done, all the meat, bones, and skins are carried

22.text: into the tent and hung over the poles, so that the sleeping-room is completely

23.text: screened off as by a curtain. The cross-stretchers of the tent are put in place,

24.text: and the outer covering is tightened to the utmost. A leg-joint is bound with

25.text: willow to the stretcher standing over the sleeping-room. To this is tied some

26.text: “food of the soil;” for instance, a root of Polygonum polymorphum or Polygo-

27.text: num viviparum. The women cook large kettles of meat, boil reindeer-heads,

29.text: After the meal, the drums belonging to the family, all of which are hung

30.text: on the tent-poles behind the curtain of raw skins, are beaten, and a shamanistic

31.text: performance begins. The drums are beaten continually the rest of the day.

32.text: Each member of the family is bound to have his turn. When the grown

33.text: people have finished, the children take their places and keep up the beating.

34.text: Many grown people, while beating the drum, call the “spirits” and try to

35.text: induce them to enter their bodies. They imitate shamans, utter the cries of

36.text: various animals, and make the peculiar noise supposed to be characteristic of

37.text: “spirits,” which is produced by a vibrating motion of the lips while the head

38.text: is shaken violently. The sound is something like prrr!

39.text: The “thin [skin] slaughtering,” besides being a family ceremonial, affords

40.text: one of the most important social holidays. In wealthy districts, neighboring

41.text: camps hold it on different days, so as to enable everybody to gather at one

42.text: camp after another. The poorer camps of the Pacific coast have not the
